comparison: F I MAE=3.8744e-15 acc=1.0000; F TIA-A MAE=5.2098e-04 acc=1.0000; F P MAE=6.2587e-01 acc=0.1000; F L MAE=6.2635e-01 acc=0.0250. P/L are worse than I and TIA-A on analog fidelity because the summing node is no longer a virtual ground.
failure_modes: Passive Rf sets Vsum to the neuron voltage. Weight currents become (Vin-Vsum)/R, so the frozen identity I=Vin*G is lost. Per-neuron G_tot makes attenuation non-global. Mesh L also loads hidden nodes and drops ReLU isolation. Divider compensation assumes dest≈0 V and is therefore inconsistent on P/L.
dominant_error: Summing-node loading: V = Rf ΣVinG / (1+Rf G_tot). Secondary: VG-designed divider compensation on a floating dest; layer-2 resistive loading on L.
physical_interpretation: Unit-cell P matches k*z (k=0.495117) and does not match z. F P vs isolated theory MAE=1.0483e-03. Charge on a capacitor is not a DC replacement for I-to-V: DC is an open circuit; transient voltage is (I/C)*t and needs a clock.
hardware_level: LEVEL 2 non-ideal behavioral (P/L are passive at the I-to-V, but still use invert VCVS and ReLU B-sources). Not LEVEL 4–6.
conclusion: PASSIVE I-TO-V CANNOT IMPLEMENT THE FROZEN MAP. A virtual-ground (TIA or 0 V dump) is a minimum active primitive for this conductance encoding. Next: make the unavoidable TIA errors ratiometric / offset-immune.
next_question: Can TIA input offset be cancelled by a matched replica so the Experiment 17 combined-MC floor (Vos-dominated) falls without reintroducing a current dump?
